Past analyses of AMZN (most recent first):

[2026-09-09 | AMZN | Overweight | -2.6% | -1.5% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Overweight

**Executive Summary**: AMZN is Overweight, but sized for an unconfirmed bottom rather than a confirmed one: start with **0.2x of a standard AMZN allocation** near $252.40 (or on a daily close above $250.65 with a bullish reversal candle), not the trader's 0.4x, and keep the rest unallocated. Build toward 1.0x only via **0.4x in the $239–$244 confluence** on stabilization or a reversal candle and **0.4x on a daily close above $260.15 with volume above 40M**, with a final 0.2x released only after the late-October Q3 print confirms operating margin ≥13.7% and capex at or below Q2's $54.2B — 1.2x maximum, no leverage. Risk controls: a close below $250.65 on >40M shares cuts the starter to 0.1x and pauses additions; the tranche-B stop is $235.40 (below the 7/30 close, ~2.6 ATR, wide because the 7/31 +$25.18 gap and the 2/6 −9.72% session are not in ATR); a daily close below $226.65 takes the position to zero. Horizon 3–6 months, re-scored on the Q3 print or on the $260.15 / $226.65 triggers, whichever comes first.

**Investment Thesis**: The direction is not close — the bull file wins on unrefuted operating arithmetic — but the size and the entry are decided by the two seats that never got answered on mechanics.

**What the conservative and the aggressive both conceded.** Nobody in the debate rebutted the operating evidence: Q2 revenue +19.6% to $200.6B, operating income +43.2% to $27.46B, operating margin +226 bp to 13.7%, gross margin 52.3%, with marketing +2.5%, G&A −6.0%, SBC −7.6% in dollars and share count +0.8% against ~19.6% revenue growth. That is genuine operating leverage, not an accounting artifact. TTM operating cash flow of $161.4B (+33%, H1 +44%), $176B of cash and AFS securities against $132.2B of total debt, roughly $30B net cash ex-leases and 20.9x interest coverage mean the bear case is a valuation-and-mix case, never a solvency case. The conservative said so himself: "I am not disputing that AMZN is a strong long-term franchise," and "we do not need positive free cash flow before buying." Once that is conceded, Sell and Underweight are off the table and the debate collapses to how much capital at what price.

**What the bear actually won, and it is why this is Overweight and not Buy.** TTM free cash flow is −$11.6B (H1 −$27.0B), capex is $173B, or 107% of operating cash flow and 27% of Q2 revenue; long-term debt rose 93% in six months to $132.2B with interest expense +155%; and reported earnings quality is poor — roughly $50.5B of the Q2 result was a non-cash markup of a private holding (that book went $16.2B → $122.3B, ~11% of assets), leaving core EPS near $1.95 for the quarter and ~$7.30 annualized, about 35x at $252.40. I also adopt the Research Manager's correction over the aggressive's framing: the $650B of contractual obligations is a commitment book with $78.1B due inside twelve months, not a revenue backlog, and it cuts both ways if AI demand disappoints. These facts do not forbid buying — they forbid buying full size before the capex-to-returns bridge is visible.

**The aggressive overreaches on entry and on risk arithmetic.** Calling a lower-band test an entry signal misreads the technical report, which classifies it as an inflection: first close below the 50-SMA ($254.68) since 7/31, price 2.01% under the 10-EMA ($257.59) and 2.45% under VWMA ($258.73), a fresh MACD zero-cross with histogram −1.33, RSI 44.06 below both August troughs with no divergence, three lower highs and a fresh leg low at $250.65, %B ≈ 0.02 with the lower band at $252.12, plus a 20-SMA falling ~$0.70/day toward a bearish cross. A 50% base-case range-digestion probability against a 30% bearish continuation case is not a pre-positioning signal. More concretely, the aggressive's claim that a 0.4x starter stopped at $235.40 risks "roughly 2.7% of a standard notional… that is defined risk, not recklessness" survives only if you never translate it into equity: on the plan's own calibration (1 ATR = 0.5–1.0% of equity, ATR $6.47), a $17 stop on a 0.4x tranche is 0.5–1.05% of equity for the *first* slice, and 8.1% of standard notional (~1.6–3.2% of equity) at the 1.2x maximum — and that assumes no gap through a name that moved +$25.18 on 7/31 and −9.72% on 2/6. The trader's "well under that band per tranche" is arithmetically wrong, and the conservative is the seat that caught it.

**The conservative overreaches on the prescription.** Requiring a reclaim of $254.68, then $257.59–$258.73, then $260.15 before any meaningful exposure converts a still-intact primary trend into a waiting game — giving up roughly 3% to buy confirmation while the rising 200-SMA at $239.44 sits 5.4% below spot and the 50/200 spread of $15.24 is widening. His $248 stop is inside one ATR and would be noise-hit inside the current compression; the neutral's correction is the right one — you do not tighten the stop to defeat noise, you shrink the position so the wide stop is tolerable. His 0.8x pre-Q3 cap also pre-judges the Q3 outcome rather than sizing for it. And the record is explicit: heavy AMZN underweights inside an intact rising 50/200 structure (07-22 to 07-30) cost 12–22% of five-day alpha, while the disciplined 8/27 Overweight earned +0.8%.

**The neutral wins the decisive exchange, and I adopt it.** Halve the first tranche to 0.2x, keep the wide $235.40 strategic stop, reserve the 0.4x for the $239–$244 zone (~1.2–2 ATR below spot, at the 200-SMA $239.44 / gap-top $239.82 confluence) on a confirmed reversal rather than a falling knife, require the volume-confirmed $260.15 close for the next 0.4x, and gate the final 0.2x on the Q3 print. This matches size to evidence: the tape is bearish enough that a full 0.4x starter leans on a wide stop before any stabilization prints, but the structure is intact enough (price +5.4% above a rising 200-SMA, golden cross intact, ATR compressed 35% to $6.47, volume 33.1M vs ~32.4M average — no capitulation or distribution signature, an orderly 11.1% give-back inside a 46.5% advance) that zero exposure is itself an uncompensated bet. The 9/1 AAPL lesson applies directly: stage tranches at least an ATR apart and halve the first one rather than treating a fast fill as a gift.

**What is missing, and is weighted zero.** No AWS segment revenue, operating margin or backlog, so the demand side of the $173B capex program is inference, not evidence; no implied-volatility data, so any option overlay is unpriceable and is not recommended; no insider or sentiment data; no market-cap or consensus valuation inputs; and no portfolio, holdings or cash context, so every multiplier is a fraction of a caller-defined standard AMZN sleeve — and AMZN should be counted as one AI-capex-correlated position alongside any NVDA or hyperscaler exposure already held. If the caller is already at target AMZN weight, this is a hold with the $239–$244 confirmed-reversal zone as the only add.

**What would change the call.** Up to Buy requires the capex-to-returns bridge to appear: Q3 operating margin at or above 13.7% while capex prints at or below Q2's $54.2B, D&A/revenue stabilizing near 10%, TTM free cash flow turning positive, disclosure of a genuine AWS backlog or AI-revenue figure, a first upward or at least stable mark on the $122.3B private book, and a volume-confirmed close above $260.15 followed by $266.40–$268.18. Down to Hold/Underweight on a close below $250.65 on >40M shares that fails to reclaim within two to three sessions (cut the starter to 0.1x), any markdown in that private equity book (a size-reduction event, not a dip to buy), a break of the rising 200-SMA, or net cash crossing to net debt while capex stays above $50B/quarter. A daily close below $226.65 ends the primary-trend case and takes the position to zero rather than to the stop.

**Price Target**: 266.0

**Time Horizon**: 3-6 months, re-scored on the late-October Q3 print or on the $260.15 / $226.65 triggers, whichever comes first

REFLECTION:
The −1.5% five-day alpha (−2.6% raw) says the entry timing was wrong-footed, but five days against a 3–6 month horizon can only test the starter tranche, not the operating thesis. It undercuts the claim that "zero exposure is itself an uncompensated bet" — the technical inflection read (RSI below both August troughs with no divergence, fresh MACD zero-cross at −1.33, %B ≈ 0.02) deserved more than the 50% range-digestion weight it got, and the 0.2x sizing was the only thing that made the miss cheap. Lesson for next time: when a momentum inflection and a widening 50/200 spread pull in opposite directions, price the first tranche at the inflection rather than at the trend, and treat a lower-band tag as a wait-for-confirmation event rather than a starter trigger.

[2026-09-08 | AMZN | Underweight | -3.3% | -2.2% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Underweight

**Executive Summary**: AMZN moves to below-benchmark weight: trim roughly one-third to one-half of the current position to about 0.6x–0.7x standard allocation, keeping a core rather than exiting. Execute the majority of the reduction near market at $256.97 now, with the balance as limits into $258.74–$261.14 — do not queue the primary trim above spot, and do not add anywhere inside the $254–$257 mid-range. Risk control is closing-basis only: a daily close below $251.93 on volume above 42M cuts the core by another third to half, with $245–$246 then $240.14 as the next trim zones and the $235.50 gap floor treated as a tail scenario to be survived by sizing. Re-risk in stages — a first close above $261.14 on >42M with price above the 10-EMA/VWMA and the MACD histogram positive restores at most one-quarter to one-third of the trimmed amount; full weight requires follow-through plus fundamental evidence. If already below benchmark weight, do nothing and add nothing. Horizon 1–3 months, re-scored on the late-October Q3 print.

**Investment Thesis**: All three risk seats and the Research Manager converge on reducing AMZN at $256.97, so the decision is execution, not direction — and the neutral analyst's calibration wins, with one correction taken from the aggressive seat and from the AMZN record.

Why this is a trim and not a Sell/exit. The operating engine and the primary trend are intact and unrefuted: 2Q26 revenue $200.61B at +19.6%, operating income $27.46B at +43.2%, margin 13.69% (+226bp); 1H26 OCF $71.42B (+44.2%); $176.11B of cash and AFS securities; 20.9x interest coverage; 50-day SMA $254.435 above the 200-day $239.295, both rising, spread +6.3%, price above both; and the decline is benign drift — 29.4M shares versus a ~32.4M 20-day average — with the MACD histogram improving three sessions running (-1.354, -1.179, -1.120) and $251.93 holding on a closing basis. The conservative analyst's demand to cut to ≤0.5x standard and take the core to a minimal residual on the first close below $251.93 over-corrects against exactly this; the record shows heavy AMZN de-risking inside an intact rising 50/200 structure repeatedly forfeited five-day alpha.

Why the trim, sized as it is. The entry point is the least informative price on the chart: $256.97 sits between the $251.93/$254.435 support stack and the $258.743 10-EMA / $259.567 VWMA / $261.141 falling Bollinger-mid cluster inside a 6.79% bandwidth squeeze, making the $254–$257 zone a no-add zone in both directions. The tape tilts negative — 16 of 18 closes below the 10-EMA, lower highs unbroken from $287.20 to $257.99, MACD decayed from 8.432 to 0.118 with the signal cross fired 08-17, RSI 48.12 with no bullish divergence at the $251.93 low, and the 08-28 spike to $267.56 sold into supply at $266–268. The business side is a trajectory problem, not a level problem: 1H26 FCF -$26.99B and -$66.76B after acquisitions; capex $98.41B at +72% y/y and 25.8% of revenue; acquisitions $39.77B versus $1.65B; $67.00B of long-term debt issued roughly equal to the funding gap; adjusted net debt including leases $66.65B from $37.76B; net cash $51.49B to $29.67B; interest coverage halved from 37.2x to 20.9x; current ratio 1.03x; receivables +53.4% to $88.09B against +19.6% revenue; and $50.49B of non-cash mark-ups equal to 80.6% of 2Q26 net income and 94.6% of non-operating income, on a $122.30B nonmarketable equity book at 11.2% of assets. The bull's FCF defense rests on a capex inflection not in evidence, and no valuation multiple or consensus estimate was supplied to act as a cushion.

Where each seat loses. The aggressive analyst is right that the trim is cheap to be wrong on a closing basis (about 1.6 points to $261.14, under a third of ATR 6.483) but wrong to make $259.57 the primary entry: with the NTSB scope on 21Air/Amazon live and the Sanders/Casar bill naming AMZN, both unpriced across a Labor Day close, requiring strength into $258.74–$261.14 assumes liquidity in precisely the way he faults the neutral for assuming it at the break — and the 08-28 AMZN review already documented an above-spot tranche producing no fills while the residual carried full exposure. The conservative analyst is right that a risk-reduction plan must not wait for a better price, and right that a single close above a falling Bollinger mid is not proof of demand — hence a staged quarter-to-third re-risk rather than restore-on-one-close — but wrong on magnitude, since his own evidence (operating income +43.2%, OCF +44.2%, $176.11B liquidity, 20.9x coverage) does not justify a punitive floor or a near-exit at a level 1.0% below spot. The bear overreaches on capex-as-defense: segment revenue and operating income were absent, so that question cannot be settled either way, and Thiel's position and the Walmart/Costco discount are sentiment, not catalysts.

What would change it. Up: a close above $261.14 on >42M with the 10-EMA turning up through the VWMA at $259.567 and the MACD histogram positive, followed by a session holding above $261.14 — restored in stages, then full weight only on 3Q26 capex rolling below ~$50B/quarter, TTM FCF turning positive, segment disclosure showing AWS revenue/margin accelerating, or a transaction validating the $122.30B book. A capitulation flush into $245–$246 or $240.14 that reverses on heavy volume is a legitimate secondary add, but only after the reversal prints. Down: escalating NTSB contractor-oversight findings or committee action/co-sponsor counts on the Sanders/Casar bill, any markdown on the nonmarketable equity book, a break of $240.14, or 3Q26 evidence that capex-to-revenue is still rising while net cash falls — each argues toward a fuller exit.

Gap risk and gaps in the data. Because $251.93 is roughly one ATR (2.52% of price) below spot and sits directly under known support inside a squeeze — a classic stop-sweep setup — it must be applied on closes, never on intraday wicks, and the core must be sized so a gap to $235.50 (over three ATRs) does not breach the caller's risk budget; a put or collar near $251.93 is a supplement for large books, never a substitute for sizing. Not underwritten and flagged to the desk: no portfolio, holdings, cost basis or cash context (all sizing is a fraction of a caller-defined standard AMZN allocation); segment revenue and operating income were absent; no valuation multiples or consensus estimates; 3Q26 capex guidance is the key missing swing input for the FCF path; news coverage was incomplete (143 of 163 eligible records not supplied, September 1–4 unrepresented); and no options-implied volatility, skew, sentiment or usable insider data was available to price the headline risk.

**Price Target**: 249.0

**Time Horizon**: 1-3 months, re-scored on the late-October Q3 print

REFLECTION:
The 5-day alpha of -2.2% vs SPY (raw -3.3%) supports the Underweight directional call, though five days is too short to judge the 1–3 month thesis. This window supports the tape read—negative momentum and supply above spot—while leaving the FCF/capex and nonmarketable-equity concerns untested. Lesson: when the tape tilts negative inside a squeeze, execute the full intended reduction at market rather than splitting it into above-spot limits that may not fill.

[2026-09-04 | AMZN | Overweight | -1.9% | -0.7% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Overweight

**Executive Summary**: AMZN is Overweight, but built in stages and capped at 1.0x standard allocation until the Q3 print confirms the capex and depreciation trajectory. Stage 1: ~0.30x at 252.00–254.50 (lower band / 9-1 low / just above the rising 50-SMA at 253.95), sized off a realistic stress stop near 248.00 rather than the idealized 2.74-point gap to the 250.76 daily-close invalidation. Stage 2: ~0.30x only on a daily close above 262.20 on ≥40M shares with a next-session hold above 259.78–262.20; Stage 3: ~0.20x only after a confirmed break-and-retest above 267.56 alongside capex or AWS segment confirmation. Do not add at 267.75 into the 267.56 trim zone — treat 267.56 and 273.63 as partial scale-out levels, keep total single-name drawdown at ≤2% of portfolio value, cut to market weight on a daily close below 250.76, reduce to Underweight below 245.00, and never average down. Horizon 3–6 months, re-scored on the Q3 print.

**Investment Thesis**: Direction goes with the operating evidence; size, entry geometry and add discipline go with the neutral analyst, whose corrections no one rebutted.

What the aggressive analyst won, unrefuted by either colleague: AMZN grew Q2 revenue +19.6% (accelerating from +16.6%), operating income +43.2% to $27.5B, operating margin +230bp to 13.7%, and TTM operating cash flow +33.2% to $161.4B — with inventory flat at $38.2B, marketing +2.5% against +19.6% revenue, and SBC down to 3.0% of revenue. Margins expanded while D&A was already running +31% y/y and capex was at peak intensity, which is operating leverage outrunning depreciation, and it is the hardest fact in the debate to explain away.
